result.coverage: Exhaustive differential sweep of every code point U+3000..U+FFFF except the surrogates U+D800..U+DFFF (51,200 code points), done TWICE with different batch alignments (300 cps/arg starting at U+3000, then 437 cps/arg starting at U+3001), 3 args per invocation so all three repr'd fields (--a key, --b/--c values) were exercised; failing batches were bisected to single code points. Both sweeps independently isolated exactly one bad code point. On top of that: (a) targeted spot groups for U+3000 ideographic space, Hangul Jamo/Compat-Jamo/Syllables + the unassigned U+D7A4..U+D7FF tail, CJK Ext-A/URO boundaries (U+3400, U+4DB5-4DBF, U+4E00, U+9FFD-9FFF), full private use area sample U+E000/E001/F000/F8FE/F8FF (Co), CJK Compat Ideographs incl. unassigned U+FA6E/FA6F/FADB, Alphabetic Presentation Forms holes (U+FB07/FB17/FB37/FB3D/FB45), the 32 noncharacters U+FDD0..U+FDEF, all 16 variation selectors U+FE00..U+FE0F, U+FE1A-FE2F/FE30-FE6F holes, Arabic Presentation Forms-B incl. U+FEFD/FEFE and U+FEFF BOM (Cf), Halfwidth/Fullwidth holes (U+FFBF-FFC1, FFC8/FFC9, FFD7, FFDD, FFE7, FFEF), and Specials U+FFF0/FFF8/FFF9/FFFA/FFFB/FFFC/FFFD/FFFE/FFFF (Cf + Cn noncharacters) — each group also placed mid-string and at string edges; (b) long-string stress: a 14,335-code-point argv value spanning U+3000..U+D7FF and a 4,096-code-point value spanning U+E000..U+FFFF, split across --a/--b/--c; (c) unicode through argparse error paths (unrecognized-argument echo of 10/60/80/100-char CJK, ideographic-space, PUA, U+FFFE and Hangul runs; missing-required-option with a 50-char CJK value; unicode long/short option names) to check usage/error wrapping, all matching. I also probed just outside the assigned dimension to characterize the single failure's root cause (U+2FFB..U+2FFF, U+31EE/U+31F0, U+2EBEF/U+2EBF0/U+2EE5D/U+2EE5E).

mismatches.title: U+31EF is printed literally by Node but escaped as ㇯ by Python (Unicode data version skew: ICU 15.1 vs CPython 3.12's 15.0)
mismatches.suspectedCause: /output/lib/py/unicode.mjs decides printability with the ECMAScript property escapes /^[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Co}\p{Cn}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Zs}]$/u, which V8 resolves against its bundled ICU Unicode tables (node 18.19.1 here reports process.versions.unicode === '15.1'). The Python reference is CPython 3.12, whose unicodedata is Unicode 15.0.0. U+31EF IDEOGRAPHIC DESCRIPTION CHARACTER SUBTRACTION was added in Unicode 15.1, so it is General_Category=So (printable, emitted literally) for Node but General_Category=Cn (unassigned -> non-printable -> ㇯) for CPython 3.12. Deriving printability from the host's live Unicode tables makes the port's repr() a function of the Node/ICU build; it needs a pinned Unicode 15.0 non-printable range table (or, minimally, an override list forcing the Unicode 15.1 additions back to non-printable). Note this also makes the port's behaviour vary across Node versions: a Node built with Unicode 15.0 would pass this case and a Node 22/24 build (Unicode 16.0) would diverge on even more code points.

result.notes:
Only one mismatch exists in the assigned U+3000..U+FFFF range, and it is a symptom of a broader class. The complete set of code points where Node's Unicode 15.1 tables disagree with CPython 3.12's Unicode 15.0 tables is exactly the Unicode 15.1 character additions, and I confirmed every one of them mismatches (each with the same literal-vs-\\u/\\U escape divergence):

  - U+2FFC, U+2FFD, U+2FFE, U+2FFF (Ideographic Description Characters) - BELOW my range, so whoever owns U+2000-U+2FFF should be seeing these. Repro: /tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xe2\xbf\xbc')" --b y --c z
  - U+31EF - reported above, in my range.
  - U+2EBF0..U+2EE5D (CJK Unified Ideographs Extension I, 622 code points) - ASTRAL, so the supplementary-plane dimension should be seeing these; Python emits \U0002ebf0 etc. Repro of the two endpoints: /tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xf0\xae\xaf\xb0')" --b y --c z  and  /tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xf0\xae\xb9\x9d')" --b y --c z
  Boundary code points on both sides (U+2FFB, U+31EE, U+31F0, U+2EBEF, U+2EE5E) all PASS, which pins the cause to the version delta rather than a range/off-by-one bug in the escaping logic.

Everything else in my dimension is byte-identical: quote selection, the \\uhhhh lowercase-hex 4-digit form, the Zs exception for U+0020 only (U+3000 correctly escaped), Co/Cf/Cn/Cs handling, noncharacters, variation selectors, and long-value/error-path formatting. The escaping algorithm in /output/lib/py/repr.mjs (reprStr) is otherwise a faithful match; the only defect is the data source used by isPrintableCodePoint in /output/lib/py/unicode.mjs.

Reproducibility caveat for the maintainer: because the bug is host-Unicode-dependent, the U+31EF repro will only FAIL on a Node whose ICU is Unicode >= 15.1 (verified here on node v18.19.1 / ICU 74.2 / unicode 15.1). It is still a real port defect - the port must not inherit its Unicode version from the runtime.

result.title: repr() printability is read from the host's live ICU Unicode tables, so all Unicode 15.1 additions (U+2FFC-U+2FFF, U+31EF, U+2EBF0, U+2EE5D) print literally in Node but are escaped by CPython 3.12 (Unicode 15.0)
result.reasoning:
CONFIRMED. I tried to refute this and could not; it is a genuine byte-level divergence reproduced through /tmp/dt.sh.

Refutation attempts, all failed:
1. Ran the reporter's exact repro via /tmp/dt.sh (not "node /output/test6.mjs"): FAIL, exit 1. So it is not a prog-name/usage-wrapping artifact.
2. Shell quoting is clean: the harness dumps argv once and passes the identical "$@" array to BOTH sides. It shows arg=[U+31EF] hex=[e387af] -- one well-formed UTF-8 sequence. Both sides provably saw the same argv.
3. Not a misread hex dump: I dumped each side separately with od -c and cat. Python emits the seven literal ASCII bytes 5c 75 33 31 65 66 ("㇯"); Node emits the three raw UTF-8 bytes e3 87 af.
4. Not a harness bug: control "/tmp/dt.sh --a x --b y --c z" PASSes, and the immediate neighbours U+31EE and U+31F0 PASS. Only the one code point diverges.

Mechanism confirmed exactly as reported. node -e reports process.versions.node=18.19.1, process.versions.unicode=15.1, v8=10.2.154.26-node.28. The port's regex at /output/lib/py/unicode.mjs:14, /^[\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Cs}\p{Co}\p{Cn}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\p{Zs}]$/u, returns false for U+31EF, so isPrintableCodePoint (line 28) reports it printable and repr() emits it raw. CPython 3.12 ships Unicode 15.0, where U+31EF is unassigned (Cn) and therefore non-printable, so str.__repr__ escapes it.

SCOPE IS BROADER THAN THE REPORT. I tested every Unicode 15.1 assignment addition individually; all diverge, and every 15.0-side neighbour passes -- the exact signature of a table-version skew, not a coincidence:
  FAIL (added in 15.1): U+2FFC, U+2FFD, U+2FFE, U+2FFF, U+31EF, U+2EBF0, U+2EE5D
  PASS (assigned in 15.0, or still unassigned in 15.1): U+2FFB, U+31EE, U+31F0, U+2EBEF, U+2EE5E, U+4DBF, U+9FFF
A single argument containing all seven failing code points reproduces them together.

ONE MINOR INACCURACY IN THE REPORT (insufficient to refute): the "claimed python output" block shows the literal character on the Python side too, byte-identical to the claimed Node output, so the reporter's own quoted evidence appears to show no difference at all -- they evidently pasted rendered/console-displayed text instead of raw bytes. The actual Python line 2 is OrderedMultiDict([('㇯', 'y')]) with a literal backslash. The bug and the diagnosed root cause are both correct.

Fix direction in the report is right: printability must come from a Unicode 15.0 non-printable range table pinned inside the port, not from the host's live ICU tables. As written, the port's repr() is a function of the Node build -- a Node built against Unicode 15.0 would pass these cases, and Node 22/24 (Unicode 16.0) would diverge on many more code points.
result.minimalRepro:
/tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xe3\x87\xaf')" --b y --c z

# broader: all 7 Unicode 15.1 additions in one argument
/tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xe2\xbf\xbc\xe2\xbf\xbd\xe2\xbf\xbe\xe2\xbf\xbf\xe3\x87\xaf\xf0\xae\xaf\xb0\xf0\xae\xb9\x9d')" --b y --c z

# adjacent code points that correctly PASS (proves it is not the harness)
/tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xe3\x87\xae')" --b y --c z
/tmp/dt.sh --a "$(printf '\xe3\x87\xb0')" --b y --c z
